title: GPU Fleet Healthboard & Surge Orchestrator — compact control path
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: operators need a single compact view to triage GPU pool health and trigger short-lived capacity bursts without leaving the console. Current dashboards are fragmented (per-pool detailed page, separate autoscale config screen). Goal: design a healthboard that surfaces fleet and pool-level signals, provides an inline surge/burst workflow, and contains a low-friction manual autoscale control for SREs and platform engineers.

Scope: compact healthline (fleet summary + top 5 pools), per-pool quick-actions (pause autoscale, request burst, set soft targets), burst modal with preflight checks, and a timeline of recent scaling events. Include keyboard shortcuts and responsive behavior for small screens.

Acceptance criteria:
- High-fidelity Figma screens for healthboard, pool flyout, and burst modal (desktop + tablet).
- Prototype with clickable burst flow for usability testing.
- ARIA labels and color contrast checks documented for WCAG 2.1 AA.
- Defined API contract doc for telemetry and action endpoints to hand back to Eng (links below).

Links and artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/redwood/dedicated-fleet-healthboard-2026 (prototype frames v1–v3)
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/2165/Dedicated+Fleet+Healthboard+PRD
- Prototype recording (usability session 1): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/healthboard-session1
- Backend contract sketch: https://docs.redwood.internal/telemetry/healthboard-api-v1.md

Constraints & considerations:
- Telemetry must include 5s aggregated latency, token throughput, GPU util, queue depth, and burst budget. Backend currently exposes 15s buckets (ENG-56789) — visual smoothing needed.
- Burst operations must be authorized and audited; tie into RBAC + audit log events (security review flagged).
- Minimize write-paths from the console; use optimistic UI patterns and server-side confirmation for long-running scale ops.

Open questions:
- Should burst budget be editable inline or only in a modal with approvals?
- How do we represent transient degradation vs sustained issues in a compact visual?

Next steps:
- Incorporate feedback from SRE working group (3/12) and update Figma frames.
- Deliver final prototype and run 6 moderated usability sessions (target complete 3/18).
- Coordinate with ENG-61234 to add 5s telemetry endpoint or implement smoothing on client if server-side change is delayed.
